newsitem.title: DENMARK: Court appeal on Danish EU challenge seen in October.
newsitem.headline: Court appeal on Danish EU challenge seen in October.

text.p: An appeal by a group of Danes challenging the legality of Denmark's European Union membership is expected to open in the Supreme Court in October, a government official said on Wednesday.
"We consider a start at that time to be realistic," Foreign Ministry legal department chief Peter Biering told a briefing.

On Friday, the High Court rejected a suit by the group of 10 charging that since joining the EU in 1973 Denmark had ceded national authority to the bloc's institutions in breach of its own constitution.
The petitioners said they would appeal and have until August 22 to file. A definitive judgment is expected at the end of this year or early in 1998.
Most analysts expect the appeal to fail but if it succeeds the government must either renegotiate all its EU treaties or amend the constitution, both long and tortuous processes.
The government has said it expects to delay a referendum on the latest revisions to the EU, agreed at a summit in Amsterdam last month, until the appeal verdict is delivered

The centre-left coalition government believes its case is watertight and lawyers from both sides say the state attorneys' task has been eased by rulings that the case should be limited to events since the EU's 1992 Maastricht Treaty.
Danes, traditionally cool toward European integration, rejected the Maastricht Treaty outright in a 1992 referendum.
Voters grudgingly approved the treaty the following year on condition that Denmark opted out of economic and monetary union and joint defence, policing and asylum policies.
